thesisQuality.note: Essential regulated grid assets, rising large-load demand and visible rate-base investment support durable value capture.

financialOperatingMomentum.note: Profitable regulated operations and raised guidance are tempered by modest Q2 EPS decline and heavy capital needs.

marketValuationOpportunity.note: Current market context supports reasonable but not distressed valuation for regulated growth.

catalystScore.note: Large-load commitments, grid approvals and rate-base deployment provide multiple identifiable multi-year catalysts.

governancePower.note: Regulated capital allocation is disciplined by commissions and guidance, though execution across a large buildout remains material.

alignment2036.note: Transmission, distribution and generation are foundational infrastructure for electrification, industry and compute demand.

crossDivisionLeverage.note: Generation, transmission and distribution serve residential, industrial and data-center demand across multiple states.

bottleneckControl.note: AEP controls regulated grid infrastructure and interconnection pathways where capacity is a real constraint.

scenarioRobustness.note: Essential utility demand and geographic/customer breadth are robust while rate, load-growth and financing scenarios matter.

substitutionResilience.note: Regulated wires and grid interconnection are difficult to bypass at scale even when generation technologies change.

supplyChainResilience.note: Scale provides planning flexibility, but turbines, transformers and permitting remain meaningful bottlenecks.

pricingPower.note: Approved rate-base returns and cost recovery provide structured value capture constrained by affordability and regulatory review.

risk.note: Capital intensity, funding costs, regulatory recovery and load-conversion risk moderated by essential infrastructure.

confidence.note: Current primary evidence covers required factors; customer-level firmness remains partly undisclosed.

thesis: AEP controls essential regulated grid infrastructure in territories seeing strong load growth, creating long-duration rate-base growth if demand converts and recovery is timely.
keyRisk: Capital can be deployed ahead of realized load or at unfavorable financing cost while regulatory constraints delay recovery.
nextCatalyst: Further conversion of large-load commitments into approved projects and updated earnings/capital guidance.
